title: mlflow.genai.review_queues on Databricks: fluent calls must be guarded with databricks_api_disabled to raise a clear error instead of a 500
answers: Why does list_review_queues return INTERNAL_ERROR Not Found on a Databricks workspace?
How do I make create_review_queue or get_or_create_user_queue fail with a clear message on Databricks?
Where is the Databricks tracking URI guard for review queues handled?
Why do label_schemas calls raise a helpful error on Databricks but review queue calls do not?
body:
Path: mlflow/genai/review_queues/__init__.py public fluent functions (create_review_queue, get_or_create_user_queue, get_review_queue, list_review_queues, update_review_queue, delete_review_queue, add_items_to_review_queue, remove_items_from_review_queue, list_review_queue_items, set_review_queue_item_status). Each one goes through TracingClient in mlflow/tracing/client.py to the OSS /api/3.0/mlflow/review-queues/* routes.
Rule: Any fluent API whose OSS route is not implemented on Databricks is wrapped with @databricks_api_disabled("<function_name>", _REVIEWS_UI_ALTERNATIVE) from mlflow/utils/databricks_utils.py:databricks_api_disabled, placed directly under @experimental. The guard raises MlflowException INVALID_PARAMETER_VALUE before any client construction or network call, so new public review_queues functions need the same decorator with the correct function name string.
Symptom: On a Databricks tracking URI, review queue calls failed with a generic RestException INTERNAL_ERROR: Not Found (HTTP 500) that looked like a server outage, not an unsupported-feature error.
Constraints: Applies when the tracking URI is Databricks (databricks or databricks://profile). The guard fires regardless of whether the workspace has the Review Queues preview enabled. Does not change behaviour on OSS tracking URIs. The pattern mirrors the existing label_schemas guardrail.
applies: Fluent APIs in mlflow.genai.review_queues (and sibling genai APIs) on Databricks tracking URIs; OSS tracking unaffected.
says: Review queue operations fail with generic internal server errors on Databricks workspaces.
Provide clear error messages explaining review queues are unsupported on Databricks tracking servers.
Managing review queues on a Databricks workspace looks like a broken server outage.
Show an actionable notice directing users to the review UI when using Databricks.
Listing or creating review queues crashes unexpectedly when connected to Databricks environments.
search: Fluent APIs in `mlflow.genai.review_queues` must be decorated with `@databricks_api_disabled` from `mlflow/utils/databricks_utils.py` to raise `MlflowException` `INVALID_PARAMETER_VALUE` on Databricks tracking URIs instead of HTTP 500 errors. The decorator wraps public functions such as `create_review_queue`, `list_review_queues`, and `get_or_create_user_queue` under `@experimental` before constructing `TracingClient` or calling `/api/3.0/mlflow/review-queues/*` routes. Applies when the tracking URI is Databricks (`databricks` or `databricks://profile`) regardless of preview status, mirroring the `label_schemas` guardrail without modifying open-source tracking behavior.
